<description>
Currently there is no test coverage for oversized CompactSize. This is fine, because a vector this large will already be rejected earlier by the P2P transport payload size check.

However, it would be good to still add test coverage:

* Removing the check would pass all tests.
* There is some accidental non-deterministic coverage through tx-deser "fuzzing", which hurts coverage reports, see https://github.com/corecheck/corecheck/pull/219#discussion_r4554170963.
* Having explicit end-to-end P2P coverage for such corrupt messages seems fine.
</description>

[2026-11-19] rc:4629925386 inline on test/functional/p2p_invalid_messages.py by maflcko (member) (edited 2026-11-19):
It is impossible to enumerate all cases of "misbehavior" and it can also be net-split risky to mark something as misbehavior when ancient (pre-bip) protocol may have allowed it.

The p2p protocol message size limit was added in ba04c4a7801e7d68a5e84035b919e5c3626eb7a7 without a bip, so making MAX_SIZE+1  compactsize a misbehavior may be controversial and difficult to review.

In any case, this is a test-only pull, so I am not allowed to change misbehavior here. Also, to give more examples, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906 goes the opposite way and changes a bad-txns-oversize from misbehavior to an ignored deser error.

To also give an example where a new misbehavior is added based on a bip text: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35550
